note_on_method: Two of the filter slugs have a lawful data driver in Wichita, and the City's own page supplies both. Its Parks tab sits under the heading "Outdoor courts with hard / concrete surfaces", its Recreation Centers tab under "Temporary indoor courts with wood and tile surfaces", and its Riverside Tennis Center tab says "outdoors" and "indoors" itself, so all ten published venues carry an indoor-or-outdoor answer in the City's words. Lights has no page: the City states lighting at one venue, Riverside, and a filter page needs three. Free has none: the City prices no venue and frees none. The page was read in a browser, because wichita.gov refuses scripted requests, and every line quoted here is asserted against the saved text.

slots.why_this_filter:
Five Wichita venues hold outdoor pickleball courts, and thirty-one of the city's fifty-three courts are at them. The City drew the line itself. Four of the five sit on the Parks tab under a heading that begins "Outdoor courts", and the fifth, Riverside Tennis Center, has its own tab that says "9 outdoors with court lights for night play". This site publishes an indoor-or-outdoor answer only when an operator states one, and Wichita states it for every venue on one page.

Outdoor and indoor are documented in opposite ways in this city. The indoor courts are temporary, laid out in a gym for drop-in sessions whose hours sit in two PDFs this site has not read. An outdoor court is there whenever the park is open, on a record that does not say when that is: no hours for any park, no lighting at four of the five, and no price anywhere. The two largest sets in Wichita, Edgemoor Park's twelve courts and Riverside's nine lit ones, are both on this side of the line.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the City of Wichita's Pickleball page places it under a heading or a line that says its courts are outdoors. Five qualify. Edgemoor Park, Buffalo Park, Osage Park and Seneca Park are the four parks on the Parks tab under "Outdoor courts with hard / concrete surfaces", with twelve, two, two and six courts. Riverside Tennis Center qualifies on the City's own line, "9 outdoors with court lights for night play".

Edgemoor is on the indoor page as well, because the Recreation Centers tab lists "Edgemoor / 5815 E 9th Street / 3 courts" at the same address as the park's twelve; the two lines publish as one venue with a count on each side. Riverside is on both pages too.

Sherwood Glen is the last line of the Parks tab, "1 striped without net (portable net required)", with no street line where every other park has one, and a venue without an address does not publish. The heading's "hard / concrete" puts no surface on any venue here: it is one sentence over four parks, and which park has which is not stated.

faqs.q: Which outdoor courts in Wichita have lights?
faqs.a: Riverside Tennis Center's nine, in the City's words "with court lights for night play". Edgemoor, Buffalo, Osage and Seneca carry no lighting statement either way, so they are recorded as not stated.

faqs.q: What are the hours at the outdoor courts?
faqs.a: Not stated. The City prints no opening or closing time for any of its four parks or for Riverside, so this site cannot say whether any of them closes at sunset.
Not stated. The City's one sentence on cost, "Some can be reserved for a small fee while others are first-come-first-serve", does not name a venue. This site does not assume a park court is free.

slots.why_this_filter:
Seven Wichita venues hold indoor pickleball courts, twenty-two courts between them, and with seven Wichita has more published indoor venues than any city on this site. The City states every one of them in its own words: six recreation centres under the heading "Temporary indoor courts with wood and tile surfaces", and Riverside Tennis Center's "6 indoors (these are double-striped over the 3 tennis courts)".

What indoor means in Wichita is specific. None of the seven is an indoor pickleball facility. Six are recreation centres whose courts the City calls temporary, laid out in a gym for drop-in sessions rather than built into the floor, and the seventh is a tennis centre whose indoor pickleball is lines painted over three tennis courts. The courts exist at certain times and not at others, and the City publishes those times in two PDFs, "View Summer Drop-In Hours" and "View Fall Drop-In Hours", that this site has not read. So an indoor venue here is a count and a phone number rather than a schedule. One of the seven, Brewer, is printed "(Closed for Improvements)" with no date.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the City of Wichita's Pickleball page places it under a heading or a line that says its courts are indoors. Seven qualify. Boston, Edgemoor, Linwood and Orchard hold three each and Evergreen and Brewer two each, all on the Recreation Centers tab under "Temporary indoor courts with wood and tile surfaces"; Riverside Tennis Center holds six on its own tab, "6 indoors (these are double-striped over the 3 tennis courts)". Twenty-two in all.

Two of the seven are on the outdoor page as well. Edgemoor's three indoor courts are in the recreation centre at 5815 E 9th, the same address as the park's twelve outdoor courts, and the two City lines publish as one venue. Brewer qualifies although the City prints it as "Brewer (Closed for Improvements)": the count is stated and the closure is printed beside it. The heading's "wood and tile" puts no surface on any venue, because it is one sentence over six centres and which centre has which floor is not stated.

faqs.q: When can I play indoors in Wichita?
faqs.a: At the drop-in times in the City's summer and fall PDFs, which this site has not read, so no session is published here. Each of the seven venues carries a phone number on the City's line; ring it.
Not stated. The City says some Wichita courts "can be reserved for a small fee while others are first-come-first-serve" and names no venue. Riverside carries a reservation link but no price.
Not on the City's page as read on 7 September 2026, which prints "Brewer (Closed for Improvements)" with no reopening date. It publishes here as closed; ring 316-337-9222 before going.

sources.not_stated: Hours at any venue beyond Brewer's closure, lighting anywhere but Riverside, a price or a free answer for any named venue, a surface for any single venue, and any address for Sherwood Glen.

sources.evidence: All ten published addresses were matched at house-number level and placed in Sedgwick County, KS, inside the incorporated place Wichita - five through the Census address file as the City writes them (Buffalo Park, Seneca Park, Boston, Linwood, Riverside Tennis Center), four through OpenStreetMap because the Census appended a compass direction the City does not write (Edgemoor Park, Osage Park, Brewer, Orchard), and Evergreen on a Census answer that drops the City's N because OpenStreetMap holds nothing for the address as written. Sherwood Glen has no address to resolve. Snapshot: data/sources/wichita-county-census.json
sources.not_stated: Anything about whether a court is indoor or outdoor.
